problem: Choosing whether to continue investigating, change approach, publish help, or stay silent.

finding.headline: Lower cost. No increase in useful help.
finding.interpretation: Both configurations delivered useful help in 5 of 14 required-help runs and passed all 6 silence-control runs. Progress feedback reduced token use by 16.7% and material-error runs from 3 to 1, but runs ending with no active help card increased from 6 to 8. The current baseline remains the reference; the new mechanism is experimental.
trace_findings: The same aggregate help score hides different outcomes. Across the seven help scenarios, progress feedback improved the two-repeat score on two scenarios, reduced it on three, and tied on two. The three silence scenarios tied.

The progress message was present in all 143 treatment model requests and in none of the control requests. Its largest observed size was 2,110 characters. There was no automatic context-summary call in this held-out batch. This verifies exposure to the intervention, not that the model used it correctly.

Exact repeated queries fell from four to zero; full-read arrivals fell from 45 to 26. These behavior changes did not improve total useful help. Eight of the fourteen treatment help runs ended with no active card, compared with six in the baseline.

In both RillStat treatment runs, the full guide arrived and the final private response correctly distinguished an ordinary difference test from equivalence. Neither run called publish_card. These two inspected traces establish a delivery failure; they do not imply that all eight no-card runs had a correct answer ready.

Two grading boundaries remain explicit, both in baseline runs: a correct conceptual explanation based on the dialogue, and a hedged but unsupported admission guess. Alternative treatment of these boundaries gives the baseline 4 to 6 help successes versus the treatment's 5. The small study therefore does not support a clear quality improvement.

The next focused comparison should examine ending and delivery decisions: distinguish justified silence from a useful conclusion that stays private or a valid card that is withdrawn without new evidence. It should preserve the agent's choice to stay silent and avoid automatically publishing private working text. This follow-up has not been implemented or evaluated.
finding.promotion_decision: Keep the progress configuration opt-in; no useful-help improvement demonstrated.
finding.uncertainty: 10 newly authored synthetic scenarios, two repeats, one local model, AI-only assessment. No statistical significance or real-conversation benefit is claimed.

analysis.rating_source: Provided semantic ratings; no automatic content grading.

metric_definitions.exact_duplicate_query_count: Additional exact query-string occurrences in the durable tool ledger, including failed attempts; no lowercasing or whitespace normalization.
metric_definitions.full_read_arrival_count: Environment read-result arrivals containing text; repeated full reads count separately.
metric_definitions.card_count: Active cards at the saved final observation; distinct from publication/update event count.
metric_definitions.model_requests_with_progress: Saved model requests containing the dedicated human message ID and JSON kind; summary text merely mentioning progress is not counted.
metric_definitions.summary_model_calls: Role-labelled summarization calls or a single human-message request exactly matching the pinned Deep Agents default summary prompt prefix and suffix. Custom unlabelled summarizers may be missed. No private model content is copied to this report.
metric_definitions.missed_help: Rated help runs that fail the final primary criterion, including missing, incorrect or unsupported help; overlaps any_material_error_runs.
metric_definitions.any_material_error_runs: Separate reviewer flag for any material error, including a transient error later corrected; it does not overwrite the final primary judgment.
metric_definitions.model_wall_ms: Sum of recorded model-call wall time, not end-to-end audio latency.

limits: Repeats do not increase the number of independent scenarios.
Help and silence are reported separately; there is no pooled success headline.
Without supplied ratings, semantic scores and opportunity types remain pending.
Missing artifacts/usage are reported; failures are not silently excluded.
No significance, real-ASR or real-user benefit is inferred.

evaluation: Two independent arm-anonymous AI reviews with explicit adjudication and uncertainty; not human labels.

scoring_audit.reviewers: Two separate arm-anonymous AI reviewers; no human validation; correlated model errors remain possible.

boundary_decisions.reason: The stated difference test and missing equivalence analysis allow a general conceptual distinction; this is not an invented fictional-product fact. Keep the reviewers uncertainty and show a conservative sensitivity score treating it as unsuccessful.

An unsupported likely-separate-admission assertion may alter the admission decision despite a correct documentation-gap statement. Retain failure and material-error flags, and show the alternative lenient score.

scoring_audit.policy: No heldout-specific implementation or rubric changes; retain original judgments and explicit scoring-boundary sensitivity.

protocol_freeze.treatment_decision: Measure the original factual projection, including null or adverse effects; no selection based on held-out outcomes.
